about.seoDescription: Learn about Africa New Generation (ANG)'s story, mission, vision, and the refugee-led leadership team building protection and opportunity in Kyaka II Settlement, Uganda.

hero.title: A Refugee-Led Movement for Protection and Opportunity
hero.subtitle: Founded by refugees, for refugees — and the communities that host them.

story.title: Our Story
body: We were founded refugees who refused to accept that displacement should mean the end of dignity, education, Livelihood and opportunity.   Our name says it all: A New Generation one that leads with compassion, resilience, and durable solutions from within the community. Kyaka II is home to over 139 000 refugees, mostly from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Years of conflict, poverty, and lack of services have left many families vulnerable. We saw children sleeping in markets. We saw persons with disabilities left behind. We saw women and youth with skills but no support. We saw a community with incredible strength, but very little resources.

In 2019, a group of youth, females, males and community volunteers came together and said: “If no one will do it for us, we will do it ourselves. That is how Africa New Generation (ANG) was born. We started with $0 funding, bicycles, and conversations under trees. We went door to door, listened. We traced families, We mediated conflicts and brought children home. Today, Africa New Generation (ANG) is recognized as one of the most active refugee and women-led organizations in Kyaka II, working in 9 zones with a team of community volunteers, social workers, and peer educators.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.body: To lead the fight against exclusion by empowering Persons with Special Needs ( including vulnerable children, girls, women, and PWDs) and youth with skills, advocacy, and linkages to opportunities that promote self-reliance and sustainable livelihoods..

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.body: An Africa where persons with special needs and youth live with dignity, independence, and hope ;  building a brighter future through self-reliance and durable solutions.

items.title: Dignity
items.description: We treat every person we serve as a whole individual with agency and worth — never as a passive recipient of aid.

items.title: Inclusion
items.description: Our programs are designed with — not just for — the people they serve, including women, youth, and persons with disabilities at every stage.

items.title: Community Leadership
items.description: We believe displaced communities are best placed to identify their own needs and lead the solutions that address them.

items.title: Transparency
items.description: We are accountable to the communities we serve and to our partners and supporters, in how we make decisions and use resources.

programs.seoDescription: Explore Africa New Generation (ANG)'s nine program areas — Child Protection, Women Empowerment, Disability Inclusion, Education, Health, Livelihood, Agriculture, Youth Development, and Climate Action.

hero.title: Our Programs
hero.subtitle: Nine areas of focus, one shared goal: dignity and opportunity for every displaced person we serve.

intro.title: Community-Led, Needs-Driven
intro.description: Each of our nine program areas was shaped directly by the communities we serve, and is delivered by teams who understand those needs firsthand.

childProtection.title: Child Protection
childProtection.shortDescription: Safeguarding vulnerable children through protection services, psychosocial support, and family reunification.
childProtection.description: Displacement puts children at heightened risk of separation from family, exploitation, and psychological harm. Our Child Protection program identifies vulnerable children early, coordinates case management and referrals, and provides psychosocial support so that every child in Kyaka II Settlement has a safe path forward.

objectives: Identify and respond to cases of child abuse, neglect, and exploitation within the settlement
Reunify separated and unaccompanied children with family wherever possible
Provide psychosocial support to children affected by trauma and displacement
Train community members as child protection focal points
activities: Community-based case identification and referral pathways
Individual and group psychosocial support sessions
Child protection awareness sessions for parents and caregivers
Safe spaces programming for young children
detail.targetBeneficiaries: Children under 18 in Kyaka II Settlement who are separated, unaccompanied, at risk of abuse or neglect, or affected by trauma — along with their caregivers and foster families.

timeline.title: Program Launch
timeline.description: Child protection case management began with a small team of community-based volunteers.

timeline.title: Safe Spaces Expansion
timeline.description: Established dedicated safe spaces for psychosocial support sessions across multiple settlement zones.

timeline.title: Formal Referral Pathways
timeline.description: Built structured referral relationships with settlement authorities and specialized service providers.

successStories.name: A Caregiver, Kyaka II
successStories.quote: When the child protection team helped us through the reunification process, our family finally felt whole again.

detail.ctaDescription: Your support helps us reach more vulnerable children with the protection and care they need.

womenEmpowerment.title: Women Empowerment
womenEmpowerment.shortDescription: Economic and social empowerment programs for refugee and host-community women.
womenEmpowerment.description: Women carry a disproportionate burden in displacement settings, often as sole caregivers with limited access to income. Our Women Empowerment program builds economic independence through savings groups, vocational training, and leadership development — while creating safe spaces for women to organize and support one another.

objectives: Increase women's access to income-generating opportunities
Build financial literacy and savings capacity through group-based models
Develop women's leadership within community structures
Strengthen support networks that reduce isolation and vulnerability
activities: Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA) group formation and training
detail.targetBeneficiaries: Refugee and host-community women in Kyaka II Settlement, with particular focus on female heads of household and young mothers.

timeline.title: First Savings Groups Formed
timeline.description: Launched the first Village Savings and Loan Associations with a small cohort of women.

timeline.title: Vocational Training Introduced
timeline.description: Added structured skills training to help members translate savings into small businesses.

timeline.title: Leadership Track Launched
timeline.description: Introduced leadership development for group leads to represent women's interests in community decision-making.

successStories.name: A VSLA Member, Kyaka II
successStories.quote: Through our savings group, I started a small shop that now supports my whole family — something I never thought possible after we fled our home.

detail.ctaDescription: Support that reaches women multiplies — strengthening whole families and communities.

disabilityInclusion.title: Disability Inclusion
disabilityInclusion.shortDescription: Ensuring persons with disabilities have equal access to protection, services, and opportunity.
disabilityInclusion.description: Persons with disabilities in displacement settings are often the most excluded from services, education, and livelihoods. Our Disability Inclusion program works to remove physical, social, and informational barriers — ensuring people with disabilities and their families are full participants in community life, not an afterthought.

objectives: Identify persons with disabilities and connect them to appropriate services
Improve physical accessibility of community spaces and learning environments
Reduce stigma through community awareness and disability-led advocacy
Support livelihood opportunities tailored to individual ability and interest
activities: Household-level disability identification and needs assessment
Provision and adaptation of assistive devices where possible
Disability-led peer support groups and community awareness sessions
detail.targetBeneficiaries: Children and adults with physical, sensory, or intellectual disabilities in Kyaka II Settlement, and their families.

timeline.title: Community Needs Assessment
timeline.description: Conducted a settlement-wide assessment to understand the scale and nature of disability-related needs.

timeline.title: Accessible Spaces Pilot
timeline.description: Adapted a first learning space for accessibility, developed with direct input from families.

timeline.title: Peer Support Network
timeline.description: Established disability-led peer groups to guide program direction and reduce community stigma.

successStories.name: A Parent, Kyaka II
successStories.quote: For the first time, my daughter has a classroom built with her needs in mind — and friends who understand her.

detail.ctaTitle: Help Build a More Inclusive Community
detail.ctaDescription: Your support helps remove barriers that keep people with disabilities from full participation in community life.

youthDevelopment.title: Youth Development
youthDevelopment.shortDescription: Mentorship, skills-building, and leadership development for young people.
youthDevelopment.description: Young people in Kyaka II Settlement represent both the population most affected by disrupted education and the community's greatest source of future leadership. Our Youth Development program combines mentorship, skills training, and structured leadership opportunities to help young people build a sense of purpose and direction.

education.title: Education
education.shortDescription: Expanding access to quality education for refugee and host-community children.
education.description: Education is one of the most powerful tools for breaking cycles of displacement-driven disadvantage. We work to expand access to quality learning — supporting enrollment, providing learning materials, and advocating for children who face barriers to attending school.

health.title: Health
health.shortDescription: Improving access to essential health services in the settlement.
health.description: Access to basic health services can be inconsistent in settlement environments. Our Health program works to connect families with essential care, supports community health education, and helps address gaps in maternal and child health services.

livelihood.title: Livelihood
livelihood.shortDescription: Vocational training and income-generating opportunities for families.
livelihood.description: Sustainable income is central to long-term self-reliance. Our Livelihood program provides vocational training and support for small income-generating activities, helping families move from dependency toward stability.

agriculture.title: Agriculture
agriculture.shortDescription: Sustainable farming initiatives to strengthen food security.
agriculture.description: Many families in Kyaka II Settlement rely on small-scale farming to supplement limited food access. Our Agriculture program introduces sustainable farming techniques and supports access to seeds and tools to strengthen household food security.

climateAction.title: Climate Action
climateAction.shortDescription: Community-led environmental protection and climate resilience projects.
climateAction.description: Environmental degradation compounds the challenges displaced communities already face. Our Climate Action program supports tree-planting, sustainable land use, and community education on environmental stewardship and climate resilience.

hero.title: Impact Stories
hero.subtitle: Stories of resilience and transformation from the people we serve.

items.title: From Missed Classrooms to a Path Forward
items.excerpt: After two years without formal schooling, Amina is back in the classroom — and dreaming about what comes next.
items.quote: I used to think school was something that happened to other children. Now I know it can happen to me too.
body: When Amina's family arrived in Kyaka II Settlement, getting her enrolled in school felt like an impossible task — missing documents, no uniform, and a family focused entirely on survival. For two years, her education was on hold.

Through Africa New Generation (ANG)'s Education program, our team worked with Amina's family to resolve enrollment barriers, provided basic learning materials, and connected her with a peer support group of other children catching up after displacement.
Today, Amina attends school regularly and has started talking about becoming a teacher herself one day — so she can help other children the way she was helped.

items.title: Building a Business From Nothing
items.excerpt: A carpentry apprenticeship gave James more than a skill — it gave his family a stable income for the first time since displacement.
items.quote: I learned to build furniture. What I really built was a future for my children.
body: James arrived in Kyaka II Settlement with years of informal carpentry experience but no way to put it to use — no tools, no workshop, no clients.

Through Africa New Generation (ANG)'s Livelihood program, James received a structured vocational training refresher, a starter set of tools, and support connecting with his first paying customers within the settlement.
Eighteen months later, James now trains two apprentices of his own and supplies furniture to households across multiple settlement zones.

items.title: Finding Family Again
items.excerpt: Separated from her family during their journey, Grace was reunited with her mother after a six-month search led by our protection team.
items.quote: I stopped believing I would ever see my mother again. Then one day, she was standing right in front of me.
body: Grace was separated from her mother during a chaotic border crossing. She arrived in Kyaka II Settlement alone, placed temporarily with a foster family identified through our child protection network.
Our case workers began a family tracing process, coordinating with protection actors across the region. After six months, Grace's mother was located in a different settlement.
The reunification process included careful preparation and psychosocial support for both Grace and her mother, ensuring the transition back together was safe and sustainable.

items.title: A Classroom Built for Him
items.excerpt: Peter, who uses a wheelchair, had never attended school before an accessible learning space opened near his home.
items.quote: My son comes home every day excited to tell me what he learned. I never imagined this was possible.
body: Peter has used a wheelchair since early childhood. For years, the nearest school was physically inaccessible, and his family had largely given up on the idea of formal education for him.

When Africa New Generation (ANG)'s Disability Inclusion program adapted a nearby learning space — widening doorways, building a ramp, and training teachers on inclusive methods — Peter enrolled for the first time.
He now attends class daily alongside other children, supported by a peer group that grew from the same program.

items.title: A Savings Group, A Second Chance
items.excerpt: Esther joined a Village Savings and Loan Association with nothing to save. A year later, she runs a small tailoring business.
items.quote: We didn't just save money together. We rebuilt our confidence together.
body: As a single mother of four, Esther arrived in Kyaka II Settlement with no stable income and few options. She joined one of Africa New Generation (ANG)'s first Village Savings and Loan Associations, contributing what little she could each week.
Alongside the savings group, Esther completed a tailoring skills course through our Women Empowerment program and used her first loan cycle to purchase a sewing machine.
She now takes on regular tailoring work from across the settlement and has become a mentor to newer members of her savings group.

items.title: From Borrowed Land to Food Security
items.excerpt: With training in sustainable farming techniques, Moses turned a small plot of borrowed land into a reliable food source for his family.
items.quote: We used to worry about every meal. Now, for the first time, we grow enough to share with our neighbors.
body: Moses had farmed before displacement, but the small plot available to his family in Kyaka II Settlement seemed too limited to matter. Through Africa New Generation (ANG)'s Agriculture program, he received training in sustainable, space-efficient farming techniques along with a starter kit of seeds and tools.
Applying new techniques like intercropping and composting, Moses significantly increased his yield within a single growing season.
His family now has a more reliable food supply, and Moses has begun sharing surplus produce and techniques with neighboring households.
